definition: Outstar is an output from the neurodes of the hidden layer of the neural network architecture which works as an input for output layer.
details: Neurode of hidden layer provides input to neurode of the output layer.

explainer.lead: Outstar is the signal a hidden-layer neurode passes forward as input to a neurode in the output layer. It marks the point where hidden representations become outputs.

tiers.eli5: Think of a relay race: the hidden layer hands the baton to the output layer, and the baton passed is the outstar.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers trace outstar values when debugging a network to see what the hidden layer actually feeds the output layer. A pitfall is assuming these values are meaningful on their own, since they only matter relative to the output layer's weights.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the outstar is the activation vector produced by a hidden-layer neurode that serves as the input vector to an output-layer neurode; no broader guarantees about its properties are specified.

explainer.example: In a two-layer network, a hidden neurode computes an activation after its transfer function, and that value is the outstar delivered to each output neurode.
